translations.text: John the Evangelist, Christ's darling, was taken up on this day, through God's visitation, to the joy of the kingdom of heaven.
He was the son of Christ's mother's sister, and Christ loved him especially, not so much for their kinship as for the purity of his unbroken virginity.
He was chosen by God in virginity, and he remained in unblemished virginity forever.
It is read in historical narratives that he wished to take a wife, and Christ was invited to his wedding. Then it happened that the wine ran out at the wedding.
The Saviour then commanded the servants to fill six stone vessels with clear water, and with his blessing he turned the water into excellent wine.
This is the first sign that he openly worked in his humanity. Then John was so moved by that sign that he at once left his bride in her virginity,
and he always followed the Lord after that, and the Lord loved him dearly, because he had withdrawn himself from the lusts of the flesh.
Truly, the Saviour entrusted his mother to this beloved disciple when, hanging on the cross, he redeemed mankind;
so that his chaste life might take care of the chaste virgin Mary, and she then remained in the care of her sister's son.
Later, after Christ's ascension to heaven, a cruel emperor reigned over the empire of the Romans after Nero; he was called Domitian, a persecutor of Christian people:
he ordered a vat to be filled with boiling oil, and ordered the renowned evangelist to be thrust into it; but through God's protection he came out of the hot bath unharmed.
Then, when the cruel one could not suppress the blessed apostle's preaching, he sent him into exile on an island called Patmos, so that he would die there from the sharpness of hunger.
But the Almighty Saviour did not leave his beloved apostle uncared for. In that exile he showed him the revelation of things to come, about which he wrote the book called the Apocalypse:
and in that same year the cruel Domitian was killed at the hands of his counsellors; and they all agreed unanimously that all his decrees should be annulled.
Then Nerva, a very gracious man, was chosen as emperor. With his consent the apostle, who had been sent into exile with contempt, returned with great honour.
Men and women ran to meet him, rejoicing and saying, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of God."
As the apostle John was stepping into the city of Ephesus, the body of a widow was being carried toward him for burial; her name was Drusiana.
She had been very devout and eager in giving alms, and the poor, whom she had fed entirely with a generous heart, followed the body, sorrowful and weeping.
Then the apostle ordered the bier to be set down, and said, "My Lord, the Saviour Christ! May he raise you up, Drusiana; arise, and go home, and prepare a meal for us in your house."
Drusiana then arose as if woken from sleep, and, mindful of the apostle's command, went home.
On the next day the apostle was walking along the street, when he saw a philosopher leading two brothers, who had turned all their parents' wealth into precious gems,
and wanted to smash them in the sight of all the people, as a spectacle, as if in contempt of worldly possessions.
It was the custom at that time that those who wished to study worldly wisdom diligently would exchange their property for gemstones and then break them;
or in some golden ingot, and to throw it into the sea, lest the thought of their possessions should hinder them from the teaching.
Then the apostle called the philosopher Crato to him, and said, "It is foolish for anyone to despise worldly riches for the praise of men, and be condemned in God's judgement.
Useless is the medicine that cannot heal the sick; so also useless is the teaching that does not heal the sins and vices of the soul.
Truly my teacher Christ taught a certain young man who desired eternal life with these words: that he should sell all his wealth,
and distribute their value to the poor if he wished to be perfect, and he would afterwards have his treasure in heaven, and eternal life besides."

Then Crato the philosopher answered him, "These gems have been smashed for vain boasting, but if your teacher is the true God, join these fragments back together whole, so that their value may benefit the poor."
John then gathered the fragments of the gems, and looked up to heaven, saying thus, "Lord Saviour, nothing is difficult for you;
in your faithful you have restored this broken world through the sign of the holy cross;
restore now these precious gems, through the hands of your angels, so that these ignorant people may recognize your powers and believe in you."
Lo, then suddenly the gems became so whole that not even a trace of the earlier smashing could be seen.
Then the philosopher Graton, together with the young men, fell at John's feet, believing in God. The apostle baptized him with all his household, and he began to preach faith in God openly.
Then the two brothers, Atticus and Eugenius, gave away their gems and distributed all their possessions to the poor, and followed the apostle; and a great multitude of believers also joined him.
Then at one time the apostle came to the city of Pergamum, where the aforementioned young men had formerly lived, and they saw their servants adorned with fine silk and shining in worldly glory.
Then they were pierced through with the devil's arrows and became sad at heart, because they went about in poverty in a single mean cloak while their servants were shining in worldly glory.

Then the apostle perceived this devilish deceit and said, "I see that your mind has changed, and your countenance, because you distributed your riches to the needy and followed the teaching of my Lord.
Go now, therefore, to the wood, and each of you cut a burden of rods and bring them to me." They did as he commanded, and in God's name he blessed the green rods, and they were turned into red gold.
Again the apostle John said, "Go to the seashore and fetch me pebbles."
They did so; and John then blessed them by God's majesty, and they were changed into precious gems.
Then the apostle said, "Go to the smithies and test this gold and these gems."
Then they went, and came back again, saying, "All these goldsmiths say that they have never before seen gold so pure or so red;
the gem-workers also say that they have never found such precious gems."
Then the apostle said to them, "Take this gold and these gems, and go and buy yourselves landed property, since you have lost the heavenly riches.
Buy yourselves silken tunics, so that for a little while you may shine like a rose, so that you may quickly wither. Be flourishing and wealthy for a time, so that you may be poor forever.
Listen: cannot the Almighty Ruler bring it about that he makes his servants rich in this world, abounding in wealth, and shining beyond compare?
But he has set a contest for faithful souls, so that those who despise transitory riches for his name may believe that they will possess the eternal riches.
You healed the sick in the Saviour's name, you put devils to flight, you gave sight to the blind, and you healed every kind of disease;
now this gift has been taken away from you, and you who were renowned and strong have become wretches.
So great a fear of you came upon the devils that at your command they left the possessed whom they had afflicted; now you fear devils. The heavenly possessions are common to us all.
Naked we were born, and naked we depart. The brightness of the sun, and the light of the moon and of all the stars are common to the rich and to the lowly.
Showers of rain, and the church door, baptism and the forgiveness of sins, receiving the Eucharist, and God's visitation are common to all, poor and prosperous;
but the unhappy miser wants to have more than suffices him, when he does not even enjoy his abundance free from care.
The covetous man has one body and many garments; he has one belly, and food enough for a thousand men.

Indeed, because of the vice of covetousness he cannot give what he hoards to anyone else, and he does not know for whom he hoards it; as the prophet said, 'Every man is troubled in vain who hoards and does not know for whom he gathers it.'
Truly, he is not the lord of his possessions when he cannot share them out; rather he is the servant of his possessions when he serves them entirely;
and besides this, illnesses grow in his body, so that he cannot take food or drink.
He worries day and night that his wealth be kept safe; he greedily watches over his tillage, his rents, his buildings; he robs the poor; he follows his lusts and his pleasures.
Then suddenly he departs from this world, naked and guilty, carrying only his sins with him; therefore he must suffer eternal punishment."
Even as the apostle was speaking this teaching, a certain widow was carrying the body of her son to be buried; he had been married thirty days before.
The grieving mother, wailing together with the bearers, then threw herself down at the holy apostle's feet, begging him to raise her son in God's name, as he had done for the widow Drusiana.
Then John pitied the mother and the grief of the bearers, and stretched his body on the ground in long prayer; and at last he rose, and again prayed for a long time with his hands raised up.
When he had done this three times, he ordered the young man's body to be unwrapped, and said, "O young man, who through the lust of your flesh quickly lost your soul;
O young man, you did not know your Creator; you did not know the Saviour of men; you did not know the true friend; and therefore you have run into the hands of the worst enemy.

now I have shed my tears and prayed earnestly for your ignorance, that you may rise from death and make known to these two brothers, Atticus and Eugenius, how great a glory they have lost and what punishment they have earned."
With that the young man Stacteus rose, fell at John's feet, and began to rebuke the brothers who had gone astray:
saying, "I saw the angels who watched over you weeping sorrowfully, and the accursed demons rejoicing in your destruction.

"The kingdom of heaven was prepared for you, and shining dwellings filled with feasts and with eternal light; these you lost through heedlessness, and you have won for yourselves dark dwellings filled with dragons.
and with crackling flames, filled with unspeakable torments, and with horrible stenches; in it groaning and wailing do not cease, by day or by night:
Therefore pray with your inmost heart to this apostle of God, your teacher, that he raise you from eternal perdition as he raised me from death;
and that he lead your souls, which are now blotted out of the book of life, back again to God's grace and mercy."

Then the young man Stacteus, who had risen from death, together with the brothers, threw himself down at John's footprints, and all the people along with them, praying with one mind that he would intercede for them with God.

Then the apostle commanded the two brothers to offer to God thirty days of penance in repentance, and during that time to pray earnestly that the golden rods might turn back to their former nature, and the gemstones to their worthlessness.
After the space of thirty days, when they could not by their prayers turn the gold and the gemstones back to their nature, they came weeping to the apostle,

saying, "You have always taught mercy, and that people should show mercy to one another; and if people show mercy to one another, how much more will God show mercy and grace to men, the work of his hands!
What we sinned in with covetous eyes, we now repent with weeping eyes."
Then the apostle answered, "Carry the rods to the wood and the stones to the seashore: they are turned back to their nature."
When they had done this, they received God's grace again, so that they drove out devils, healed the blind and the sick, and performed many miracles in the Lord's name, just as they had done before.
The apostle then turned to God the whole land of Asia, which is reckoned as half of the world. And he wrote the fourth book of Christ, which deals most of all with Christ's divinity.

The other three evangelists, Matthew, Mark and Luke, had written earlier about Christ's humanity. Then heretics sprang up in God's church and said that Christ did not exist before he was born of Mary.
Then all the bishops of the people asked the holy apostle to compose the fourth book [the fourth Gospel] and to quench the presumption of the heretics.
John then ordered a common fast of three days. After the fast he was so greatly filled with God's Spirit that he [surpassed?] all God's angels and all created things, [?]
rose above with a lofty mind, and began the Gospel text with these words: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and so on:"

that is, in English: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. This was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and nothing was created without him."

And so on through the whole of the gospel text he made known much about Christ's divinity: how he is eternally begotten of his Father without beginning, and reigns with him in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever without end.
He wrote little about Christ's humanity, because the other three evangelists had set it out fully in their books.
It happened on a certain occasion that the idol-worshippers who were still unbelievers said that they wanted to force the apostle into their heathenism.
Then the apostle said to the heathen worshippers, "Go all together to God's church, and all call on your gods to make the church fall down by their power. Then I will turn to your heathenism.
But if the power of your gods cannot overthrow the holy church, I will overthrow your temple through the power of Almighty God, and I will smash your idols.
and then it will be judged right that you turn away from your error and believe in the true God, who alone is Almighty."
The heathen worshippers agreed to this proposal, and John urged the people with gentle words to move away from the devil's temple.
And in a clear voice he cried out in front of them all, "In God's name, let this temple fall down, with all the idols that dwell in it,
so that this crowd may know that this idolatry is the worship of the devil." Then suddenly the temple collapsed down to its foundations, and it and all its images were turned to dust.
On that same day twelve thousand heathen people were converted to the faith of Christ and consecrated by baptism.
Then the chief heathen priest still refused with great perversity, and said that he would not believe unless John drank poison and overcame the deadly drink through God's power.
Then the apostle said, "Even if you give me poison, it will not harm me, through God's name."
Then the heathen priest Aristodemus said, "You must first see others drink it and die at once, so that at least your heart may be afraid of the deadly drink."
John answered him, "If you are willing to believe in God, I will take the drink without fear."
Then Aristodemus went to the proconsul and took two thieves from his prison, and gave them the poison in front of all the people, in John's sight; and right after the drink they died.

Afterwards the heathen priest also gave the poisonous drink to the apostle. He armed his mouth and his whole body with the sign of the cross, adjured the poison in God's name, and then with a confident mind drank it all.

Then Aristodemus and the people watched the apostle for three hours of the day, and saw that his face was cheerful, without pallor or fear; and they all cried out, "There is one true God, the one whom John worships."
Then the heathen priest said to the apostle, "I still have doubts. But if you raise these dead criminals in your God's name, then my heart will be cleansed of every doubt."
Then John said, "Aristodemus, take my tunic and lay it over the bodies of the dead men, and say, 'The apostle of the Saviour Christ has sent me to you,
that you may rise from death in his name, and that every man may know that death and life serve my Saviour.'"
Then, at the apostle's command, he carried his tunic and laid it on the two dead men; and they immediately rose up whole.
When the heathen priest saw that, he threw himself down at John's feet. Afterwards he went to the chief magistrate and told him about the miracles in a loud voice.
Then they both came to the apostle, begging his mercy. The apostle ordered them to fast for seven nights, and afterwards baptized them;
After their baptism they threw down all their idols. With the help of their kinsmen, and with all their skill, they built a great church to God in the apostle's honour.
When the apostle was ninety-nine years old, the Lord Christ appeared to him with the other apostles whom he had taken from this life, and said, "John, come to me;
it is time for you to feast with your brothers at my banquet." Then John rose and went toward the Saviour;
but he said to him, "Now on Sunday, the day of my resurrection, you will come to me"; and after these words the Lord returned to heaven.

The apostle rejoiced greatly at the promise. Early on the Sunday, before dawn, he came to the church. From cockcrow until the third hour he taught the people what they owed to God, and he sang mass for them.
He said that the Saviour had invited him to heaven on that day. Then he ordered his grave to be dug beside the altar and the earth to be carried out.
He went alive and well into his grave, stretched out his hands and called to God: "Lord Christ, I thank you for inviting me to your feast. You know that I have longed for you with all my heart.
I often asked you to let me go to you, but you told me to wait, so that I could win more people for you.
You kept my body from every defilement. You always gave light to my soul, and you never abandoned me anywhere.
You set the word of your truth in my mouth, and I wrote down the teaching that I heard from your mouth, and the wonders that I saw you work.
Now, Lord, I entrust to you your children, whom your church, virgin and mother, has brought forth for you through water and the Holy Spirit.
Receive me among my brothers, with whom you came and invited me. Open the gate of life to me, so that the princes of darkness do not meet me.
You are Christ, the Son of the living God. At your Father's command you healed the world, and you sent us the Holy Spirit.
We praise you and thank you for your many blessings, throughout endless ages. Amen."
After this prayer a heavenly light appeared above the apostle inside the tomb. It shone so brightly for an hour that no man's sight could look at the radiance of that light;
And with that light he gave up his spirit to the Lord who had invited him into his kingdom.
He departed from this present life as free from the pain of death as he had been a stranger to bodily corruption.
Afterwards his tomb was found filled with manna. Manna was the name of the heavenly food that fed the people of Israel for forty years in the wilderness.
Now that food was found in John's tomb, and nothing else; and the food is still growing in it to this present day.
Many miracles were shown there. Through the apostle's intercession the sick were healed and people were set free from all dangers.
The Lord Christ grants them this. To him be glory and honour, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever without end. Amen.
